sanskrit: aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvaḥ sacivaiḥ saha lakṣmaṇaṃ kupitaṃ śrutvā mumocāsanam ātmavān
english: Having heard the words of Aṅgada, and having heard that Lakṣmaṇa was enraged, the self-possessed Sugrīva rose from his seat together with his counsellors.

sanskrit: sacivān abravīd vākyaṃ niścitya gurulāghavam mantrajñān mantrakuśalo mantreṣu pariniṣṭhitaḥ
english: Skilled in counsel and thoroughly versed in deliberation, he weighed the gravity and lightness of the matter and spoke these words to his ministers who were wise in counsel.

sanskrit: na me durvyāhṛtaṃ kiṃ cin nāpi me duranuṣṭhitam lakṣmaṇo rāghavabhrātā kruddhaḥ kim iti cintaye
english: "I have spoken no ill word, nor have I done anything amiss. Why then is Lakṣmaṇa, the brother of Rāghava, angered? This I ponder."

sanskrit: asuhṛdbhir mamāmitrair nityam antaradarśibhiḥ mama doṣān asaṃbhūtāñ śrāvito rāghavānujaḥ
english: "By my ill-wishers and enemies, who ever seek to sow discord, Rāghava's younger brother has been made to hear of faults in me that do not exist."

sanskrit: atra tāvad yathābuddhi sarvair eva yathāvidhi bhavadbhir niścayas tasya vijñeyo nipuṇaṃ śanaiḥ
english: "In this matter, you must all carefully and methodically ascertain the true state of things, each according to his understanding and with due deliberation."

sanskrit: na khalv asti mama trāso lakṣmaṇān nāpi rāghavāt mitraṃ tv asthāna kupitaṃ janayaty eva saṃbhramam
english: "Indeed I have no fear of Lakṣmaṇa, nor of Rāghava; yet a friend angered without proper cause does indeed cause anxiety."

sanskrit: sarvathā sukaraṃ mitraṃ duṣkaraṃ paripālanam anityatvāt tu cittānāṃ prītir alpe 'pi bhidyate
english: "In every way it is easy to acquire a friend but difficult to maintain that friendship; for because of the inconstancy of minds, affection is sundered even by a trifle."

sanskrit: atonimittaṃ trasto 'haṃ rāmeṇa tu mahātmanā yan mamopakṛtaṃ śakyaṃ pratikartuṃ na tan mayā
english: "For this very reason I am afraid regarding the great-souled Rāma: that the benefit he has conferred upon me I am unable to repay."

sanskrit: sugrīveṇaivam uktas tu hanumān haripuṃgavaḥ uvāca svena tarkeṇa madhye vānaramantriṇām
english: When Sugrīva had spoken thus, Hanumān, foremost among the monkeys, spoke his own reasoned counsel in the assembly of the monkey ministers.

sanskrit: sarvathā naitad āścaryaṃ yat tvaṃ harigaṇeśvara na vismarasi susnigdham upakārakṛtaṃ śubham
english: "In every respect it is no wonder, O lord of the monkey host, that you do not forget the auspicious act of deep affection and service rendered to you."

sanskrit: rāghaveṇa tu śūreṇa bhayam utsṛjya dūrataḥ tvatpriyārthaṃ hato vālī śakratulyaparākramaḥ
english: "By the heroic Rāghava, casting fear far aside, Vālin — whose prowess equalled Indra's — was slain for your sake alone."

sanskrit: sarvathā praṇayāt kruddho rāghavo nātra saṃśayaḥ bhrātaraṃ sa prahitavāṃl lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmivardhanam
english: "Without any doubt Rāghava is angry out of affection; it is for that reason he has dispatched his brother Lakṣmaṇa, the increaser of glory."

sanskrit: tvaṃ pramatto na jānīṣe kālaṃ kalavidāṃ vara phullasaptacchadaśyāmā pravṛttā tu śarac chivā
english: "You have been negligent and do not perceive the season, O best of those who know the proper time: the auspicious autumn has arrived, dark-green with flowering saptacchada trees."

sanskrit: nirmala grahanakṣatrā dyauḥ pranaṣṭabalāhakā prasannāś ca diśaḥ sarvāḥ saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca
english: "The sky is clear, its planets and stars unclouded; the storm-clouds have dispersed; all the quarters, the rivers and the lakes are bright and serene."

sanskrit: prāptam udyogakālaṃ tu nāvaiṣi haripuṃgava tvaṃ pramatta iti vyaktaṃ lakṣmaṇo 'yam ihāgataḥ
english: "Yet you do not recognise the season of effort that has arrived, O foremost of monkeys. It is manifest that you are heedless — and so Lakṣmaṇa has come here."

sanskrit: ārtasya hṛtadārasya paruṣaṃ puruṣāntarāt vacanaṃ marṣaṇīyaṃ te rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "The harsh words of the great-souled Rāghava — who is afflicted and whose wife has been stolen — spoken through an intermediary, must be endured by you."

sanskrit: kṛtāparādhasya hi te nānyat paśyāmy ahaṃ kṣamam antareṇāñjaliṃ baddhvā lakṣmaṇasya prasādanāt
english: "For one who has committed an offence such as yours, I see no other fitting course save joining your palms and propitiating Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: niyuktair mantribhir vācyo avaśyaṃ pārthivo hitam ata eva bhayaṃ tyaktvā bravīmy avadhṛtaṃ vacaḥ
english: "A king must inevitably be told what is for his benefit by the ministers he has appointed; and so it is that, setting fear aside, I speak these resolute words."

sanskrit: abhikruddhaḥ samartho hi cāpam udyamya rāghavaḥ sadevāsuragandharvaṃ vaśe sthāpayituṃ jagat
english: "For Rāghava, when truly enraged and raising his bow, has the power to bring the entire world — gods, asuras, and gandharvas included — under his sway."

sanskrit: na sa kṣamaḥ kopayituṃ yaḥ prasādya punar bhavet pūrvopakāraṃ smaratā kṛtajñena viśeṣataḥ
english: "He who must afterwards be propitiated again ought not to be provoked; especially so by one who is grateful and remembers the prior benefit received."

sanskrit: tasya mūrdhnā praṇamya tvaṃ saputraḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ rājaṃs tiṣṭha svasamaye bhartur bhāryeva tadvaśe
english: "Bowing your head before him, together with your son and your allies, O king, abide by your own covenant and remain under his command, as a wife obeys her husband."

sanskrit: na rāmarāmānujaśāsanaṃ tvayā kapīndrayuktaṃ manasāpy apohitum mano hi te jñāsyati mānuṣaṃ balaṃ sarāghavasyāsya surendravarcasaḥ
english: "The command of Rāma and Rāma's younger brother, joined with the authority of the lord of monkeys, cannot be set aside even in thought; for your mind will come to know the human might of this Rāghava, who blazes with the splendour of Indra."

sanskrit: atha pratisamādiṣṭo lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā praviveśa guhāṃ ghorāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ rāmaśāsanāt
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, having been duly announced, entered the fearsome cavern-city of Kiṣkindhā by the command of Rāma.

sanskrit: dvārasthā harayas tatra mahākāyā mahābalāḥ babhūvur lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve prāñjalayaḥ sthitāḥ
english: The great-bodied and mighty monkeys stationed at the gate, upon seeing Lakṣmaṇa, all stood with their palms joined in reverence.

sanskrit: niḥśvasantaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā kruddhaṃ daśarathātmajam babhūvur harayas trastā na cainaṃ paryavārayan
english: Seeing the son of Daśaratha breathing heavily with rage, the monkeys became frightened and did not surround him.

sanskrit: sa taṃ ratnamayīṃ śrīmān divyāṃ puṣpitakānanām ramyāṃ ratnasamākīrṇāṃ dadarśa mahatīṃ guhām
english: The glorious Lakṣmaṇa beheld that vast and divine cavern, filled with jewels, adorned with flowering groves, charming, and strewn all about with gems.

sanskrit: harmyaprāsādasaṃbādhāṃ nānāpaṇyopaśobhitām sarvakāmaphalair vṛkṣaiḥ puṣpitair upaśobhitām
english: It was crowded with mansions and palace-towers, beautified by merchandise of every kind, and adorned by flowering trees bearing all desired fruits.

sanskrit: devagandharvaputraiś ca vānaraiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ divya mālyāmbaradhāraiḥ śobhitāṃ priyadarśanaiḥ
english: It was graced by monkeys who were sons of gods and gandharvas, shapeshifters wearing divine garlands and garments, delightful to behold.

sanskrit: candanāgarupadmānāṃ gandhaiḥ surabhigandhinām maireyāṇāṃ madhūnāṃ ca saṃmoditamahāpathām
english: Its broad avenues were suffused with the fragrances of sandalwood, agaru, and lotuses, and with the sweet scents of maireyā liquors and honey.

sanskrit: vindhyamerugiriprasthaiḥ prāsādair naikabhūmibhiḥ dadarśa girinadyaś ca vimalās tatra rāghavaḥ
english: Rāghava saw there multi-storeyed palaces resembling the slopes of Vindhya and Meru, and clear mountain streams as well.

sanskrit: aṅgadasya gṛhaṃ ramyaṃ maindasya dvividasya ca gavayasya gavākṣasya gajasya śarabhasya ca
english: He saw the charming mansions of Aṅgada and Mainda, of Dvivida, Gavaya, Gavākṣa, Gaja, and Śarabha;

sanskrit: vidyunmāleś ca saṃpāteḥ sūryākṣasya hanūmataḥ vīrabāhoḥ subāhoś ca nalasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: of Vidyunmālin, Saṃpāti, Sūryākṣa, Hanūmat, Vīrabāhu, Subāhu, and the great-souled Nala;

sanskrit: kumudasya suṣeṇasya tārajāmbavatos tathā dadhivaktrasya nīlasya supāṭalasunetrayoḥ
english: of Kumuda, Suṣeṇa, Tāra, Jāmbavat, Dadhivaktra, Nīla, Supāṭala, and Sunetra.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ kapimukhyānāṃ rājamārge mahātmanām dadarśa gṛhamukhyāni mahāsārāṇi lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa saw the principal dwelling-places of these great-souled monkey chiefs, standing along the royal road, vast and of great substance.

sanskrit: pāṇḍurābhraprakāśāni divyamālyayutāni ca prabhūtadhanadhānyāni strīratnaiḥ śobhitāni ca
english: They shone white as autumn clouds, adorned with divine garlands, filled with abundant wealth and grain, and beautified by women of surpassing excellence.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇa tu śailena parikṣiptaṃ durāsadam vānarendragṛhaṃ ramyaṃ mahendrasadanopamam
english: Surrounded by a white rocky hill and thus impregnable, the charming abode of the lord of monkeys resembled the dwelling of great Indra.

sanskrit: śulkaiḥ prāsādaśikharaiḥ kailāsaśikharopamaiḥ sarvakāmaphalair vṛkṣaiḥ puṣṭitair upaśobhitam
english: It was adorned with bright, towering palace-summits resembling the peaks of Kailāsa, and by well-nourished trees bearing all desired fruits.

sanskrit: mahendradattaiḥ śrīmadbhir nīlajīmūtasaṃnibhaiḥ divyapuṣpaphalair vṛkṣaiḥ śītacchāyair manoramaiḥ
english: Gifted by great Indra, the magnificent trees resembling dark rain-clouds bore divine flowers and fruits, gave cool shade, and were wondrously beautiful.

sanskrit: haribhiḥ saṃvṛtadvāraṃ balibhiḥ śastrapāṇibhiḥ divyamālyāvṛtaṃ śubhraṃ taptakāñcanatoraṇam
english: Its gateway was guarded by powerful monkeys armed with weapons, was bright and pure, wreathed in divine garlands, and its archway was of burnished gold.

sanskrit: sugrīvasya gṛhaṃ ramyaṃ praviveśa mahābalaḥ avāryamāṇaḥ saumitrir mahābhram iva bhāskaraḥ
english: The mighty son of Sumitrā entered the charming abode of Sugrīva, unhindered, like the sun entering a great cloud.

sanskrit: sa sapta kakṣyā dharmātmā yānāsanasamāvṛtāḥ praviśya sumahad guptaṃ dadarśāntaḥpuraṃ mahat
english: The righteous Lakṣmaṇa passed through seven inner courtyards filled with vehicles and seats, and then beheld the vast and well-guarded inner apartments.

sanskrit: haimarājataparyaṅkair bahubhiś ca varāsanaiḥ mahārhāstaraṇopetais tatra tatropaśobhitam
english: It was adorned throughout with beds of gold and silver, with many excellent seats, and furnished with coverings of the highest quality.

sanskrit: praviśann eva satataṃ śuśrāva madhurasvaram tantrīgītasamākīrṇaṃ samagītapadākṣaram
english: As he continued to enter, he heard without pause a melodious sound — a song composed of well-formed syllables, mingled with lute music.

sanskrit: bahvīś ca vividhākārā rūpayauvanagarvitāḥ striyaḥ sugrīvabhavane dadarśa sa mahābalaḥ
english: The mighty Lakṣmaṇa saw many women of varied forms in Sugrīva's palace, proud of their beauty and youth.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvābhijanasaṃpannāś citramālyakṛtasrajaḥ varamālyakṛtavyagrā bhūṣaṇottamabhūṣitāḥ
english: He observed them to be of noble birth, wearing garlands of many-hued flowers, occupied with making choice garlands, and adorned with the finest ornaments.

sanskrit: nātṛptān nāti ca vyagrān nānudāttaparicchadān sugrīvānucarāṃś cāpi lakṣayām āsa lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa observed that Sugrīva's attendants too were neither unsatisfied nor overly agitated, and were attired in noble dress.

sanskrit: tataḥ sugrīvam āsīnaṃ kāñcane paramāsane mahārhāstaraṇopete dadarśādityasaṃnibham
english: Then he saw Sugrīva seated on a supreme golden throne spread with the finest covering, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: divyābharaṇacitrāṅgaṃ divyarūpaṃ yaśasvinam divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ mahendram iva durjayam divyābharaṇamālyābhiḥ pramadābhiḥ samāvṛtam
english: His body was adorned with divine ornaments, his form was divine, his fame resplendent; wearing divine garlands and garments, he was unconquerable as great Indra, and surrounded by women decked in divine ornaments and garlands.

sanskrit: rumāṃ tu vīraḥ parirabhya gāḍhaṃ varāsanastho varahemavarṇaḥ dadarśa saumitrim adīnasattvaṃ viśālanetraḥ suviśālanetram
english: The heroic Sugrīva, tawny as fine gold, seated on his splendid throne and holding Rumā in a close embrace, caught sight of the undaunted Lakṣmaṇa of wide eyes — he himself wide-eyed.

sanskrit: tam apratihataṃ kruddhaṃ praviṣṭaṃ puruṣarṣabham sugrīvo lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā babhūva vyathitendriyaḥ
english: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa, that bull among men, enter unimpeded and in a rage, Sugrīva was seized with distress in all his senses.

sanskrit: kruddhaṃ niḥśvasamānaṃ taṃ pradīptam iva tejasā bhrātur vyasanasaṃtaptaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ daśarathātmajam
english: Seeing the son of Daśaratha — breathing in rage, blazing as it were with energy, scorched by anguish over his brother's misfortune —

sanskrit: utpapāta hariśreṣṭho hitvā sauvarṇam āsanam mahān mahendrasya yathā svalaṃkṛta iva dhvajaḥ
english: the foremost of monkeys leapt up, abandoning his golden throne, like the great well-adorned banner of Mahendra rising aloft.

sanskrit: utpatantam anūtpetū rumāprabhṛtayaḥ striyaḥ sugrīvaṃ gagane pūrṇaṃ candraṃ tārāgaṇā iva
english: As Sugrīva leapt up, Rumā and the other women rose after him, as a cluster of stars follows the full moon across the sky.

sanskrit: saṃraktanayanaḥ śrīmān vicacāla kṛtāñjaliḥ babhūvāvasthitas tatra kalpavṛkṣo mahān iva
english: The glorious Sugrīva, his eyes flushed red, approached with palms joined and stood there like a great wish-fulfilling tree.

sanskrit: rumā dvitīyaṃ sugrīvaṃ nārīmadhyagataṃ sthitam abravīl lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddhaḥ satāraṃ śaśinaṃ yathā
english: Then the angry Lakṣmaṇa addressed Sugrīva, who stood in the midst of the women with Rumā at his side, as if addressing the moon ringed by its stars.

sanskrit: sattvābhijanasaṃpannaḥ sānukrośo jitendriyaḥ kṛtajñaḥ satyavādī ca rājā loke mahīyate
english: "A king endowed with valour and noble birth, compassionate, with his senses mastered, grateful, and truthful in speech — such a king is honoured in the world."

sanskrit: yas tu rājā sthito 'dharme mitrāṇām upakāriṇām mithyāpratijñāṃ kurute ko nṛśaṃsataras tataḥ
english: "But what king is more cruel than one who abides in unrighteousness and makes a false promise to friends who have rendered him service?"

sanskrit: śatam aśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ tu gavānṛte ātmānaṃ svajanaṃ hanti puruṣaḥ puruṣānṛte
english: "A falsehood concerning a horse destroys a hundred; a falsehood concerning a cow destroys a thousand; but a man who utters a falsehood concerning a man destroys himself and all his kindred."

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ kṛtārtho mitrāṇāṃ na tat pratikaroti yaḥ kṛtaghnaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sa vadhyaḥ plavageśvara
english: "He who, his purpose having been served, does not requite his friends — that ingrate deserves to be slain by all beings, O lord of the leaping ones."

sanskrit: gīto 'yaṃ brahmaṇā ślokaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ dṛṣṭvā kṛtaghnaṃ kruddhena taṃ nibodha plavaṃgama
english: "This verse was sung by Brahmā himself, revered by all the worlds — uttered in wrath upon beholding an ingrate. Hear it, O monkey."

sanskrit: brahmaghne ca surāpe ca core bhagnavrate tathā niṣkṛtir vihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ
english: "For the slayer of a brahmin, for the drunkard, for the thief, for the one who has broken his vow — the righteous have prescribed expiation; but for an ingrate there is no expiation."

sanskrit: anāryas tvaṃ kṛtaghnaś ca mithyāvādī ca vānara pūrvaṃ kṛtārtho rāmasya na tat pratikaroṣi yat
english: "You are ignoble, ungrateful, and a speaker of falsehood, O monkey — for having had your purpose served by Rāma, you do not requite him for it."

sanskrit: nanu nāma kṛtārthena tvayā rāmasya vānara sītāyā mārgaṇe yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ kṛtam icchatā
english: "Surely you, O monkey, having had your purpose served, ought — if you truly wish to act rightly — to exert yourself in the search for Sītā on Rāma's behalf."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ grāmyeṣu bhogeṣu sakto mithyā pratiśravaḥ na tvāṃ rāmo vijānīte sarpaṃ maṇḍūkarāviṇam
english: "Yet you are absorbed in vulgar pleasures and have given a false promise. Rāma did not know you to be like a serpent that merely croaks like a frog."

sanskrit: mahābhāgena rāmeṇa pāpaḥ karuṇavedinā harīṇāṃ prāpito rājyaṃ tvaṃ durātmā mahātmanā
english: "O sinful one, you of wicked soul were given sovereignty over the monkeys by the greatly blessed and compassionate Rāma, that great-souled one."

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ cen nābhijānīṣe rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ sadyas tvaṃ niśitair bāṇair hato drakṣyasi vālinam
english: "If you do not acknowledge the deed done by Rāma, whose actions are tireless, you will this very moment, struck by his sharp arrows, behold Vālin."

sanskrit: na ca saṃkucitaḥ panthā yena vālī hato gataḥ samaye tiṣṭha sugrīva mā vālipatham anvagāḥ
english: "The path by which Vālin went after being slain has not grown narrow. Abide by your covenant, Sugrīva; do not follow the path of Vālin."

sanskrit: na nūnam ikṣvākuvarasya kārmukāc cyutāñ śarān paśyasi vajrasaṃnibhān tataḥ sukhaṃ nāma niṣevase sukhī na rāmakāryaṃ manasāpy avekṣase
english: "Surely you do not see the arrows — thunderbolt-like — released from the bow of that foremost scion of the Ikṣvākus; it is only therefore that, at ease, you indulge in pleasures and do not attend even in mind to Rāma's cause."
